section_map.heading: ## Summary

section_map.heading: ## 1. Q1: Architecture and lifecycle

section_map.heading: ## 4. Q4: Security and trust

claim_checks.claim: It removed the `initialize` handshake and protocol-level sessions ✅[3]
claim_checks.page_says: Remove protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from the Streamable HTTP transport. ... Make MCP stateless: remove the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake.
claim_checks.note: Changelog lines 153 and 155 state both removals.

claim_checks.claim: Version negotiation (experiment E2): the same server was sent `protocolVersion:"1.0.0"` and answered `"protocolVersion":"2025-11-25"`, matching the "respond with another supported version" rule ✅[4][E2]
claim_checks.page_says: If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports.
claim_checks.note: The rule part is grounded in [4] (2025-11-25 lifecycle). The observed exchange itself comes from local experiment E2 and is not checkable.

claim_checks.page_says: To discover available tools, clients send a tools/list request. This operation supports pagination and caching.
claim_checks.note: The cell sits in the 'Legacy (2025-11-25)' column but cites only [14], the 2026-07-28 tools page ('Version 2026-07-28 (latest)'); grep for '2025-11-25', 'legacy', 'previous' on that page finds nothing. A page for another version does not support a version-labelled claim.

claim_checks.claim: `notifications/tools/list_changed`, delivered on a GET stream or the open connection ✅[4][13] (Legacy (2025-11-25) column)
claim_checks.page_says: listChanged: Support for list change notifications (for prompts, resources, and tools) ... The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.
claim_checks.note: The cited 2025-11-25 pages [4] support list-change notifications for tools and a GET SSE stream, but never name the method `notifications/tools/list_changed` (searched 'list_changed', 'notifications/tools'). [13] names it only for the 2026-07-28 subscriptions/listen stream; its legacy paragraph (line 505) does not name it. The name for the legacy era is stated only in the uncited [4a-sess] (2025-11-25 security_best_practices, line 455). A claim true per an uncited cached page is unsupported; the method name is a name gap.

claim_checks.page_says: To discover available tools, clients send a tools/list request. This operation supports pagination and caching.
claim_checks.note: tools/call appears as the method of the call examples (lines 278, 337).

claim_checks.page_says: Tools in MCP are designed to be model-controlled, meaning that the language model can discover and invoke tools automatically
providing a tools array and optional toolChoice configuration in their sampling requests. ... Clients MUST declare support for tool use via the sampling.tools capability
claim_checks.note: The page also says servers MUST NOT send tool-enabled sampling requests to clients without sampling.tools, which matches the 'when' condition.

claim_checks.claim: **stdio.** The client launches the server as a subprocess; messages are newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout and must not contain embedded newlines; the server may log to stderr and must write nothing else to stdout ✅[12][4]
claim_checks.page_says: Messages are delimited by newlines, and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines. ... The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message.
claim_checks.note: Both [12] (2026-07-28 stdio) and [4] (2025-11-25 transports) also say the client launches the server as a subprocess and the server MAY write to stderr for logging; the claim is unlabelled by era and both eras' pages support every part.

claim_checks.claim: server must validate `Origin`, 403 if invalid; local servers should bind to 127.0.0.1 ✅[4] (2025-11-25 column)
claim_checks.page_says: If the Origin header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden. ... When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1)
claim_checks.note: The claim drops the condition 'present': the page requires 403 only when an Origin header is present and invalid, not when it is absent. Validation MUST and the SHOULD bind are stated correctly.

claim_checks.claim: `subscriptions/listen` (2026-07-28) or GET stream (legacy) ✅[15][4] (row: need server push of tool-list changes)
claim_checks.page_says: It replaces the former resources/subscribe RPC and the HTTP GET endpoint. ... The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.
claim_checks.note: [15] lists toolsListChanged as a listen filter and says listen replaces the HTTP GET endpoint; [4] (2025-11-25) has the optional GET SSE stream carrying server notifications.

claim_checks.claim: Alternative transports must follow established best practice for their protocol ✅[26]
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol.
claim_checks.note: The claim drops the qualifier 'security' (all best practice instead of security best practices), and the page's leading condition 'When supported:' (only when authorization is implemented). Modal strength matches.

claim_checks.claim: Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired gives `401`; insufficient scope gives `403` with `error="insufficient_scope"` and a `scope` listing what the operation needs ✅[26]
claim_checks.page_says: Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response. ... insufficient scope during runtime operations, the server SHOULD respond with: - HTTP 403 Forbidden status code
claim_checks.note: The leading 'must' covers every clause, and the flow is introduced as 'steps are normative unless marked'. Token validation, audience check and 401 are MUST on the page, but the 403 insufficient_scope response and the scope parameter are SHOULD. A SHOULD raised to MUST level.

claim_checks.claim: The tools page adds: a handle on an authenticated server "is a name, not a capability"; validate authorization on every call; state the retention policy in the creating tool's description ✅[14]
claim_checks.page_says: For authenticated servers, a handle is a name, not a capability. The server should validate the caller’s authorization against the handle on every call.
claim_checks.note: The quote is exact, but the page marks this section 'non-normative guidance for tool design' and uses 'should' for both validating on every call and stating the retention policy ('retention policy should be stated in the creation tool’s description'). The claim gives them as plain imperatives with no modal.

conflicts.topic: Whether any feature has been removed: 3.2 says 'No feature has been removed yet' citing [21], while 2.2 lists methods removed in 2026-07-28 citing [3]. The sources agree: [21] says 'No features have been removed under this policy yet' (SEP-2596 lifecycle). The doc dropped the qualifier, so the two statements read as contradicting each other.
conflicts.winner: [3] rank 1 and [21] rank 1 read with its qualifier

violations.evidence: S3: 1.6 table, Legacy (2025-11-25) column, '`tools/list` ✅[14]' cites only the 2026-07-28 tools page; no cited page covers 2025-11-25.
S4: 1.6 table, Legacy column, names `notifications/tools/list_changed` for 2025-11-25 citing [4][13]; neither names that method for the legacy era. Only the uncited [4a-sess] does.
S12: 3.5 step 9 puts the insufficient-scope 403 and its scope parameter under a leading 'must'; [26] says the server SHOULD respond with 403 and SHOULD include the needed scopes.
S9: 3.1 Origin row (2025-11-25) says '403 if invalid'; [4] says 403 only 'If the Origin header is present and invalid'.
S11: 3.5 Scope says alternative transports must follow 'established best practice'; [26] says 'established security best practices', and only 'When supported'.
S13: 4.5 gives 'validate authorization on every call; state the retention policy' as plain imperatives; [14] marks the section non-normative and uses 'should' for both.

Found in the conflict audit, outside the claims.json sample and not counted in factual_grounding: 3.2 'No feature has been removed yet ✅[21]' drops the page's qualifier 'under this policy', and as written it contradicts 2.2's removals in 2026-07-28 per [3] (handshake, ping, logging/setLevel, notifications/roots/list_changed).

The body is organized by question (Q1 to Q4), not by role. No section of its own for role 2 (concept architecture) or role 4 (worked examples); role 1 lives only in the Summary envelope. Each Q-section mixes concept, mechanism, reference, runs and decision tables (e.g. 1.1 Roles inside a mechanism section; MRTR mechanism inside the primitives catalog; transport and auth decision tables 3.4 and 3.6 inside a mechanism section). The content itself is strong: the runs show real inputs and outputs, and 3.4 and 3.6 are proper decision tables.

The heading promises reproduction, but the kept note says the experiment folders and outputs were not kept, and the absolute temporary path given no longer exists. The section is a provenance record, not a reproduction guide.
